trace.reasoning: The patient presents with yellow discoloration of the palms and soles. The supplied image (MM-1172-a.jpeg) shows a hand with diffuse, generalized yellowing of the skin, consistent with jaundice. This finding supports Hyperlipidemia type III, which can cause eruptive xanthomas and xanthelasma, often presenting with yellowish skin changes. While Syphilis causes palmar/plantar lesions, the image shows diffuse color change rather than discrete papules or plaques, making it less likely.
